stories.headline: 34 Leading AI Startups Hit ~$80B Annualized Revenue, with Anthropic and OpenAI Taking 89%

key_facts.fact: A group of 34 leading AI startups is generating nearly $80 billion in annualized revenue, equivalent to about $6.6 billion per month from selling AI products.
Total annualized revenue across these 34 firms is up 112% from six months ago, with Anthropic and OpenAI together capturing 89% of the total.
Anthropic and OpenAI are widening the revenue gap between themselves and the rest of the AI startup field.

stories.headline: Anthropic to Brief Financial Stability Board on Mythos Vulnerabilities Found in Global Finance

key_facts.fact: Anthropic agreed to brief members of the Financial Stability Board on cybersecurity vulnerabilities its Mythos model has been identifying in the global financial system, at the request of FSB chair and Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey.
When directed to develop working exploits in internal testing, Mythos reportedly succeeded on the first attempt in more than 83% of cases.
Anthropic has not publicly released Mythos and is currently running it under 'Project Glasswing,' a controlled-access programme limiting who can run the model and against what targets.
Anthropic describes Mythos as a cybersecurity model and has claimed it has found thousands of high-severity flaws across major operating systems and browsers.

stories.headline: Apple Doubles MacBook Neo Order, Books New A18 Pro Run as Binned-Chip Strategy Hits Limits

key_facts.fact: Apple is repurposing chips with partially defective cores — chips initially built for iPhones — for cheaper devices such as the $599 MacBook Neo, one of dozens of Apple products that use lower-performing processors.

Apple has now placed new A18 Pro orders with TSMC after demand for the MacBook Neo doubled the initial production target to about 10 million units, exhausting the supply of binned chips left over from the iPhone 16 Pro.
The MacBook Neo uses A18 Pro chips with five working GPU cores instead of six, salvaged from production yields that did not meet iPhone 16 Pro specifications.

stories.headline: Apple's Revamped Siri to Ship as Beta with Auto-Deleting Chats, Gurman Reports

key_facts.fact: Apple's new standalone Siri app in iOS 27 will include privacy features unique to the chatbot market and may launch as a beta test even after a two-year delay, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.
The new Siri will include an auto-deleting chats feature modeled on iMessage — users can choose to remove conversations after 30 days, one year, or keep them indefinitely.
The standalone Siri app is expected to be powered by Google Gemini and offer a ChatGPT-style chatbot experience with stricter limits on how long user information is used and stored.
Internal iOS 27 test versions use a 'beta' label on the new Siri and include a toggle to leave the beta, suggesting Apple may keep the unfinished branding through public release this fall.

stories.headline: Baidu Q1 Tops Estimates as Core AI Revenue Jumps 49%, Cloud Infra Up 79%

key_facts.fact: Baidu reported Q1 2026 revenue of 32.08 billion yuan, ahead of the 31.49 billion yuan consensus estimate, with adjusted profit of 12.06 yuan per ADR vs 11.84 yuan forecast.
Baidu Core AI-powered business revenue rose 49% year over year to 13.6 billion yuan and exceeded half of Baidu General Business revenue for the first time.
Cloud infrastructure revenue surged 79% year-on-year to 8.8 billion yuan in Q1, with GPU cloud revenue more than tripling, up 184%.
Apollo Go delivered 3.2 million driverless rides in the quarter, with triple-digit growth in fully-driverless rides as the robotaxi unit expanded internationally.

stories.headline: Bannon and 60+ MAGA Allies Urge Trump to Mandate Government Testing of Frontier AI

key_facts.fact: A group of more than 60 Trump allies — including Steve Bannon, Amy Kremer and Brendan Steinhauser — signed a letter organized by Humans First urging Trump to require mandatory testing and government approval of powerful AI systems before release.
The letter compares frontier AI to nuclear systems and aviation, citing potential to assist in designing bioweapons, breaking into critical infrastructure, or manipulating financial markets.
Bannon told Axios the letter 'takes us next level' and 'lays out [that] we must have mandatory testing and government approval.'

Humans First's tagline is 'technology should serve humans … not replace them,' and the letter supports policies requiring mandatory testing, evaluation, vetting, and government approval of potentially dangerous frontier AI systems before deployment.

stories.headline: China's CXMT Q1 Profit Soars 1,688% to $3.6B as Global Memory Crunch Tightens

key_facts.fact: ChangXin Memory Technologies reported Q1 2026 revenue up roughly 719% year-on-year to about $7.5 billion, with net profit up 1,688% to $3.6 billion.
CXMT cited Omdia data placing it fourth in global DRAM with a 7.67% share, up from a low-single-digit share a year earlier.
The company forecast first-half 2026 revenue of 110-120 billion yuan, driven by expanded output, higher DRAM prices and an improved product mix.
CXMT is preparing a Shanghai STAR Market IPO targeting roughly CNY 29.5 billion (US$4.2 billion), drawing significant interest from foreign investors.

stories.headline: GDS-Linked DayOne Plans $5B Dual IPO on Singapore and Nasdaq at ~$20B Valuation

key_facts.fact: DayOne, the international spinoff of China's largest data center operator GDS Holdings, is planning a simultaneous Singapore and US listing to raise about $5 billion, according to the Financial Times.

The listing would be one of the first to use Singapore Exchange's new Global Listing Board, which lets companies with at least $2 billion market cap list on both exchanges using a single prospectus; DayOne is expected to debut at around $20 billion.
DayOne operates roughly 480MW of in-service or under-construction data center capacity plus another 590MW reserved for development across Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia and Singapore.

DayOne raised $2 billion in a Series C in January led by Coatue, with backers including the Indonesia Investment Authority; JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America and Citigroup are working on the IPO.

stories.headline: FDA approves AstraZeneca-Daiichi Enhertu for two HER2+ early breast cancer indications

key_facts.fact: On May 17 the FDA approved Enhertu (fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki) for two new HER2-positive early breast cancer indications, covering neoadjuvant (pre-surgery) use based on DESTINY-Breast11 and adjuvant (post-surgery) use based on DESTINY-Breast05.

In DESTINY-Breast05, Enhertu cut the risk of invasive disease recurrence or death by 53% versus T-DM1 in patients with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy (HR=0.47; 95% CI 0.34–0.66; p<0.0001); three-year IDFS was 92.4% vs 83.7%.

Enhertu is now approved for nine indications, six across both early and metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, marking its expansion into the curative-intent setting for AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo.

stories.headline: FDA approves Roche's Tecentriq for muscle-invasive bladder cancer guided by ctDNA test

key_facts.fact: On May 17 the FDA approved Tecentriq (atezolizumab) and Tecentriq Hybreza as adjuvant treatment for adults with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who have circulating tumor DNA molecular residual disease (ctDNA MRD) after cystectomy, identified by Natera's Signatera CDx assay.

Approval was based on Phase III IMvigor011, which showed Tecentriq cut the risk of disease recurrence or death (DFS) by 36% and the risk of death (OS) by 41% in patients with detectable ctDNA MRD identified via serial testing within one year of cystectomy.

IMvigor011 is the first prospective Phase III study to show that a ctDNA-guided approach to adjuvant therapy can significantly improve survival in muscle-invasive bladder cancer; the safety profile was generally consistent with prior studies.

stories.headline: GitHub Makes GPT-5.3-Codex the New Base Model for Copilot Business and Enterprise

key_facts.fact: Effective May 17, 2026, GPT-5.3-Codex became the base model for all Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise organizations, replacing GPT-4.1.
GPT-5.3-Codex is GitHub's first long-term support (LTS) model, in partnership with OpenAI, guaranteed to be available for 12 months from its launch.
GPT-5.3-Codex launched on February 5, 2026, and will remain available through February 4, 2027 for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise users.

stories.headline: 30-year Treasury yield hits 5% as oil rally fuels global bond rout, rate-hike bets surge

key_facts.fact: For the first time in two decades, the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5% as Wall Street priced in greater odds for rate hikes; US, German, Japanese and UK yields all soared while stocks tumbled amid the closed Strait of Hormuz.
Markets now price a roughly three-in-four chance for a Fed rate hike by December and see a hike as a lock by March, a reversal from late February when two quarter-point cuts were expected for 2026.
Sunday futures: Dow off 174 points (-0.35%), S&P 500 -0.26%, Nasdaq -0.32%; US oil futures up 1.75% to $107.26/bbl, Brent +1.32% to $110.70; 10-year Treasury yield climbed 1.6 bps to 4.611%.

JPMorgan predicted commercial oil inventories in the developed world could 'approach operational stress levels' by early June; Capital Economics and UBS warned stockpiles could reach 'critically low levels' by end of June.
G7 finance chiefs are set to discuss the debt selloff when they meet this week; Wednesday brings the release of the Fed's April meeting minutes.

stories.headline: Samsung Shares Jump 6.7% as Court Curbs Union Strike and Wage Talks Resume

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics shares climbed as much as 6.7% in Seoul on May 18 after the company entered last-minute wage negotiations with its largest union, aimed at averting an 18-day strike scheduled to begin May 21.

The Suwon District Court on May 18 largely granted Samsung's injunction request, ordering the union to maintain normal staffing and operations during any strike and barring it from occupying company facilities.
Each of Samsung's two main unions faces a 100 million won ($66,500) per-day penalty if it violates the restrictions; the planned walkout would involve about 50,000 workers.
Samsung produces roughly one-third of the world's DRAM and is one of only three suppliers of high-bandwidth memory used in AI accelerators, alongside SK Hynix and Micron.
Samsung began mass-producing and shipping sixth-generation HBM4 memory, with the company expecting total HBM sales to more than triple in 2026 versus 2025.

stories.headline: SK Hynix Sells Out 2026 HBM Capacity and Poaches 200 Samsung Engineers in Four Months

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix has sold out its entire 2026 high-bandwidth memory capacity and recruited about 200 engineers from Samsung over the past four months.
Nomura Securities reclassified SK Hynix from a cyclical chip producer to a structural beneficiary of the AI build-out and projected 120% upside in the stock, which is up 169% year-to-date.
Samsung's HBM4 yield is reported below 60% while SK Hynix is already hitting 80% on its 1c DRAM process, with hyperscaler customers being locked into three-to-five-year supply agreements.
Demand for specialized AI memory components is forecast to grow roughly a thousandfold over the next five years versus global supply expanding around 30% annually.

stories.headline: SpaceX Dragon CRS-34 docks at ISS with 6,500 lbs of cargo and new science experiments

key_facts.fact: At 6:37 a.m. EDT on May 17, the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft docked autonomously to the forward port of the ISS Harmony module on the 34th SpaceX commercial resupply mission for NASA, carrying nearly 6,500 pounds of food, supplies and equipment for Expedition 74.

Cargo included a new instrument to study charged particles around Earth that can impact power grids and satellites, a bone scaffold made from wood that could enable treatments for osteoporosis, and equipment to evaluate how red blood cells and the spleen change in space.

Six spaceships are now parked at the station, including CRS-34 Dragon, Crew-12 Dragon, Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL, the Soyuz MS-28 crew ship, and Progress 94 and 95 resupply ships; Dragon will remain docked about a month before splashdown in the Pacific.

stories.headline: Tata Electronics and ASML Sign Pact to Equip India's First $11B Commercial Chip Fab

key_facts.fact: Tata Electronics and ASML signed a strategic partnership for ASML to supply its lithography tools, training and supply-chain support to ramp Tata's first front-end semiconductor fab in Dholera, Gujarat.
Tata Electronics is investing about $11 billion in the 300mm Dholera plant, which is designed to produce chips for AI, automotive and mobile applications.
The signing was witnessed by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten as part of Modi's Netherlands visit on May 16.
India has eight semiconductor projects underway, including a separate $14 billion Tata Electronics facility in Gujarat, as the country pursues a domestic chip industry.

stories.headline: Torvalds Says AI Bug Hunters Made Linux Security Mailing List 'Almost Entirely Unmanageable'

key_facts.fact: In his Linux 7.1-rc4 release post on May 17, Linus Torvalds wrote that 'the continued flood of AI reports has basically made the security list almost entirely unmanageable, with enormous duplication due to different people finding the same things with the same tools.'

Torvalds said AI-detected bugs 'are pretty much by definition not secret' and that treating them on a private security list is 'a waste of time for everybody involved,' since the reporters can't see each other's duplicate reports.

Torvalds wrote 'AI tools are great, but only if they actually help, rather than cause unnecessary pain and pointless make-believe work,' and urged researchers to add value by reading the docs and creating a patch on top of what the AI did.

The kernel project added new documentation requiring AI-assisted bug reports to follow concise human-style formatting, stick to verifiable impact (no speculative theoretical consequences), and have the tool propose and test a fix before submission.

stories.headline: Trump warns Iran 'better get moving FAST' after national security meeting

key_facts.fact: Trump met with top national security officials on Saturday May 16 at his Virginia golf club to discuss the path forward on the Iran war, then warned Sunday May 17 that Tehran 'better get moving, FAST, or there won't be anything left of them'.

Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, CIA Director John Ratcliffe and special envoy Steve Witkoff attended; the meeting came hours after Trump returned from a visit to China to discuss Iran with Xi Jinping.

The Pentagon has prepared a series of military target plans should Trump decide on more strikes, including targeted strikes on energy and infrastructure sites in Iran; Trump is expected to meet again with his national security team early this week.
Pakistan's interior minister Mohsin Naqvi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other officials, Iranian media said; Pakistan has acted as the primary mediator in US-Iran peace talks.

stories.headline: Drone strike sparks fire at UAE's Barakah nuclear plant in 'dangerous escalation'

key_facts.fact: On May 17 the UAE's Defence Ministry said three drones entered the country from the 'western border direction'; two were intercepted while the third struck an electrical generator outside the inner perimeter of the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in Al Dhafra, sparking a fire.
The UAE foreign ministry called the strike an 'unacceptable act of aggression' and a 'dangerous escalation'; no injuries were reported and radiological safety levels were unaffected.

The IAEA said the strike caused a fire in an electrical generator and one reactor (unit 3) was temporarily powered by emergency diesel generators; director-general Rafael Grossi expressed 'grave concern' and called for 'maximum military restraint'.

The $20 billion Barakah plant, built with help from South Korea and online since 2020, is the only nuclear power plant in the Arab world and supplies about a quarter of UAE energy needs; this is the first time the four-reactor complex has been targeted in the war.
Saudi Arabia separately said it intercepted three drones from Iraqi airspace the same day; Qatar and Saudi Arabia condemned the UAE attack as a threat to regional stability.

stories.headline: Ukraine launches ~600-drone barrage on Russia, biggest attack on Moscow in over a year

key_facts.fact: A wave of almost 600 Ukrainian drones attacked Russia overnight, killing four people, including three in the Moscow region and one in Belgorod, with another dozen wounded.

Russia's defence ministry said air defences shot down 556 drones overnight across the country, with another 30 drones intercepted after dawn; air defences destroyed 81 drones headed for Moscow since midnight, making it the largest attack on the capital in over a year.

Ukraine's defence ministry said the strikes hit the Moscow Oil Refinery, the Solnechnogorsk oil depot, and several microelectronics manufacturing facilities for the first time; Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport reported drone debris on its territory.

Zelensky said the SBU and Ukraine's Armed Forces jointly targeted military-industrial and fuel infrastructure in Moscow Oblast and air defense systems at the Belbek military airfield in occupied Crimea, calling the strikes part of a 'shift in the balance' in Kyiv's favor.
